tagline.en: The operations chief who followed Steve Jobs and took Apple from $350 billion to $4 trillion
tagline.zh: 接替乔布斯的运营主管，把苹果从 3500 亿美元带到 4 万亿美元

label.en: Savings from the IBM, Intelligent Electronics and Compaq years (estimate)
label.zh: 在 IBM、Intelligent Electronics 和康柏工作期间的积蓄（估算）

label.en: Cash from sold Apple shares and other assets (estimate)
label.zh: 出售苹果股票所得现金及其他资产（估算）

label.en: Apple shares and unvested stock awards
label.zh: 苹果持股及未归属股票奖励

t.en: Alabama roots
t.zh: 亚拉巴马少年

desc.en: Grows up in the small town of Robertsdale, Alabama, and studies industrial engineering at Auburn
desc.zh: 在亚拉巴马州小镇罗伯茨代尔长大，在奥本大学学习工业工程

t.en: The PC trade
t.zh: PC 行业学徒期

desc.en: Twelve years in IBM's PC business, an evening MBA at Duke, then a reseller and a brief stop at Compaq
desc.zh: 在 IBM 的个人电脑业务干了十二年，读完杜克的在职 MBA，之后去了一家经销商，又在康柏短暂停留

t.en: Fixing Apple's operations
t.zh: 重整苹果运营

desc.en: Joins a struggling Apple, closes factories, cuts inventory to days and rises to chief operating officer
desc.zh: 加入困境中的苹果，关掉自有工厂，把库存压到以天计，一路升到首席运营官

t.en: After Steve Jobs
t.zh: 接棒乔布斯

desc.en: Becomes CEO, weathers doubts about innovation, launches Apple Watch and takes public stands on privacy
desc.zh: 出任 CEO，顶住“创新不再”的质疑，推出 Apple Watch，并在隐私问题上公开表态

t.en: Trillion-dollar years
t.zh: 万亿美元年代

desc.en: Apple passes $1, $2 and $3 trillion as services grow, while antitrust cases pile up on three continents
desc.zh: 服务业务壮大，苹果市值接连突破 1、2、3 万亿美元，同时三大洲的反垄断案件越积越多

t.en: Tariffs and AI
t.zh: 关税与 AI

desc.en: Negotiates with the White House over tariffs, turns to Google for AI and prepares the handover
desc.zh: 为关税与白宫周旋，在 AI 上转向与谷歌合作，并为交班做准备

t.en: Executive chairman
t.zh: 执行董事长

desc.en: Hands the CEO job to John Ternus and stays on as chairman, dealing mainly with governments
desc.zh: 把 CEO 交给约翰·特努斯，自己留任董事长，主要负责与各国政府打交道

t.en: Born in Mobile, Alabama
t.zh: 出生于亚拉巴马州莫比尔

summary.en: Timothy Donald Cook was born in Mobile, Alabama, and grew up in the nearby small town of Robertsdale.
summary.zh: 蒂莫西·唐纳德·库克出生在亚拉巴马州莫比尔，在附近的小镇罗伯茨代尔长大。

why.en: Starting point, not scored. Human capital begins at the average level for a child born in the United States.
why.zh: 起点事件，不计分。人力资本以美国同龄人的平均水平作为初始值。

src.name: Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Graduates from Auburn University in industrial engineering
t.zh: 从奥本大学工业工程专业毕业

summary.en: He earned a Bachelor of Science in industrial engineering from Auburn University in Alabama, a field built around making processes faster and less wasteful.
summary.zh: 他在亚拉巴马州的奥本大学拿到工业工程理学学士学位，这门学科研究的正是怎样让流程更快、浪费更少。

why.en: An education step: the human-capital target rises with an engineering degree. Only the year is known, so the date is year precision.
why.zh: 学历台阶：拿到工科学位，人力资本目标值上调。只能确认年份，因此日期精度为“年”。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Starts a twelve-year career in IBM's personal computer business
t.zh: 进入 IBM 个人电脑业务，一干十二年

summary.en: After Auburn he went to work for IBM's personal computer business, where he stayed about twelve years and rose to director of North American fulfillment, in charge of manufacturing and distribution for the region.
summary.zh: 离开奥本后，他进入 IBM 的个人电脑业务，在那里工作了约十二年，做到北美履约总监，负责该地区的生产和配送。

why.en: First job. A small savings line starts in the model (an estimate, since his early pay was never published) and human capital steps up.
why.zh: 第一份工作。模型里开始出现一小笔积蓄（估算值，他早年的收入从未公开），人力资本上一个台阶。

fin.en: Savings from salary enter the model as an estimate.
fin.zh: 工资积蓄以估算值进入模型。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Earns an MBA from Duke as a Fuqua Scholar
t.zh: 获杜克大学 MBA，并获评 Fuqua 学者

summary.en: While working at IBM he completed an MBA at Duke University's Fuqua School of Business and was named a Fuqua Scholar, an honor for the top students in the class.
summary.zh: 在 IBM 工作期间，他读完了杜克大学福库商学院的 MBA，并获评 Fuqua 学者——这是授予班级里成绩最好的学生的荣誉。

why.en: A second education step. The human-capital target moves up for a top business degree earned while holding a management job.
why.zh: 第二级学历台阶。一边做管理工作一边拿到名校商科学位，人力资本目标值上调。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Fuqua School of Business

t.en: Leaves IBM to run the reseller division of Intelligent Electronics
t.zh: 离开 IBM，执掌 Intelligent Electronics 的经销业务

summary.en: After about twelve years at IBM he became chief operating officer of the reseller division of Intelligent Electronics, a computer distributor. The year is inferred from the length of his IBM career; sources do not give an exact date.
summary.zh: 在 IBM 工作约十二年后，他出任电脑分销商 Intelligent Electronics 经销部门的首席运营官。年份是按他在 IBM 的工作年限推算的，资料没有给出确切日期。

why.en: A footnote in money terms, but his first job running a whole operation. Human capital steps up slightly. The date is year precision and approximate.
why.zh: 金额上只是个注脚，但这是他第一次独立掌管一整摊业务。人力资本小幅上调。日期精度为“年”，且为近似值。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Becomes vice president of corporate materials at Compaq
t.zh: 出任康柏公司物料副总裁

summary.en: He joined Compaq, then the largest PC maker in the world, as vice president of corporate materials, responsible for buying and managing its product inventory. He stayed only about six months.
summary.zh: 他加入当时全球最大的个人电脑厂商康柏，任公司物料副总裁，负责采购和管理产品库存。他只待了大约六个月。

why.en: A senior job at the industry leader raises the human-capital target. It matters mostly as the safe position he gave up a few months later.
why.zh: 在行业龙头担任高管，人力资本目标值上调。它的意义主要在于：这是他几个月后放弃的那份安稳工作。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Joins Apple as senior vice president of worldwide operations
t.zh: 加入苹果，任全球运营高级副总裁

summary.en: Steve Jobs recruited him to a company that had been losing money and was worth only a few billion dollars. Cook took charge of manufacturing and the supply chain, shut Apple's own factories and warehouses in favor of contract manufacturers, and cut inventory from months to days.
summary.zh: 史蒂夫·乔布斯把他招进了一家连年亏损、市值只有几十亿美元的公司。库克接手制造和供应链，关掉苹果自己的工厂和仓库，改用代工厂，把库存从几个月压缩到几天。

why.en: The decision that defines his career, so it is scored 5. From here the model holds a small Apple equity line next to his cash. The ownership fraction is a rough estimate of his option grants in share-equivalent terms; exact early holdings were not checked against proxy filings.
why.zh: 决定他整个职业生涯的选择，因此记 5 分。从这里起，模型在现金之外加入一小笔苹果股权。持股比例是把期权折算成等值股数后的粗略估算，早年的具体持仓没有逐一核对委托书。

fin.en: Apple equity enters the model: ownership × shares outstanding × the daily AAPL close.
fin.zh: 苹果股权进入模型：持股比例 × 总股本 × AAPL 当日收盘价。

src.name: Apple Leadership · Tim Cook
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Named chief operating officer of Apple
t.zh: 被任命为苹果首席运营官

summary.en: Apple promoted him from executive vice president of worldwide sales and operations to chief operating officer, the number-two job under Steve Jobs. He joined Nike's board of directors the same year.
summary.zh: 苹果把他从全球销售与运营执行副总裁提升为首席运营官，成为乔布斯之下的二号人物。同年他加入了耐克董事会。

why.en: The human-capital target moves to the level of a senior public-company officer. A +2% on the reputation coefficient for becoming the visible second in command.
why.zh: 人力资本目标值上调到上市公司核心高管的水平。成为公开的二把手，口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Tim Cook Named COO of Apple

t.en: Takes over day-to-day operations during Jobs's leave of absence
t.zh: 乔布斯休假期间接管日常运营

summary.en: Steve Jobs announced a leave of absence until the end of June and asked Cook to be responsible for Apple's day-to-day operations. Apple kept shipping products on schedule and its shares rose about 65% between the announcement and the end of June, when Jobs returned.
summary.zh: 乔布斯宣布休假到 6 月底，并请库克负责苹果的日常运营。这期间苹果的产品照常发布，从消息公布到 6 月底乔布斯回归，股价上涨约 65%。

why.en: The share price move is in the stock. The +3% on the reputation coefficient is for showing investors that he could run the company, which made him the expected successor.
why.zh: 股价的变化已由股票反映。口碑系数 +3%，是因为他让投资者看到自己能管好公司，从此成为公认的接班人选。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Apple Media Advisory (2009-01-14)
Yahoo Finance · AAPL price history

t.en: Named CEO of Apple as Steve Jobs resigns
t.zh: 乔布斯辞任，库克出任苹果 CEO

summary.en: Steve Jobs resigned as CEO and the board named Cook, who had again been running daily operations since January, as his successor. The board also granted him one million restricted stock units, half vesting after five years and half after ten, worth about $376 million at the time.
summary.zh: 乔布斯辞去 CEO 职务，董事会任命自当年 1 月起再次主持日常运营的库克接任。董事会同时授予他 100 万股限制性股票单位，一半五年后归属，一半十年后归属，当时价值约 3.76 亿美元。

why.en: The largest step in the model: human capital rises to the level of a top global CEO, and the ownership fraction jumps with the grant. Unvested units are counted at about half their face value, because roughly half of each tranche is withheld for taxes when it vests.
why.zh: 模型里最大的一级台阶：人力资本升到全球顶级 CEO 的水平，持股比例也因这笔授予而跳升。未归属的股票单位按面值的一半左右计入，因为每一批归属时约有一半会被扣缴税款。

fin.en: Estimated equity after the grant: about $260 million, next to roughly $140 million in cash (both estimates).
fin.zh: 授予后估算的股权价值约 2.6 亿美元，另有约 1.4 亿美元现金（均为估算）。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Steve Jobs Resigns as CEO of Apple
MacRumors · Apple awards Tim Cook 1,000,000 shares (2011-08-26)
Apple Newsroom · Apple Media Advisory (2011-01-17)

t.en: Reorganizes Apple's leadership after the Apple Maps failure
t.zh: 苹果地图失利后重组管理层

summary.en: A month after he published an apology to customers for the error-filled launch of Apple Maps, Cook announced that software chief Scott Forstall and retail chief John Browett would leave. Design, software and services were redistributed among Jony Ive, Craig Federighi and Eddy Cue.
summary.zh: 苹果地图上线后错误百出，他向用户公开致歉。一个月后，库克宣布软件负责人斯科特·福斯托和零售负责人约翰·布劳伊特离职，设计、软件和服务分别交给乔尼·艾夫、克雷格·费德里吉和埃迪·库伊。

why.en: His first public product failure as CEO, so the reputation coefficient takes -2%. The reshuffle itself was later seen as the moment he took full control of the company.
why.zh: 这是他任 CEO 后第一次公开的产品失败，口碑系数 -2%。不过这次换将后来被看作他真正掌控公司的时刻。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Apple announces changes to increase collaboration
Wikipedia · Apple Maps

t.en: Testifies to a U.S. Senate panel on Apple's offshore tax structure
t.zh: 就苹果的海外税务安排在美国参议院作证

summary.en: A Senate subcommittee reported that Apple had routed tens of billions of dollars of profit through Irish subsidiaries that paid almost no tax anywhere. Cook testified that Apple pays all the taxes it owes and called for a simpler corporate tax code.
summary.zh: 参议院一个小组委员会的报告称，苹果把数百亿美元利润转入爱尔兰子公司，这些子公司在任何地方几乎都不缴税。库克作证说苹果缴纳了全部应缴税款，并呼吁简化企业税法。

why.en: Scored as mixed. The findings hurt Apple's image, but the stock did not react. A small -1% on the reputation coefficient.
why.zh: 记为好坏参半。调查结论有损苹果形象，但股价没有反应。口碑系数小幅 -1%。

src.name: U.S. Senate PSI · Offshore Profit Shifting and the U.S. Tax Code, Part 2 (Apple Inc.)
CNBC · Tim Cook: We pay every single dollar in taxes owed (2013-05-21)

t.en: Apple agrees to buy Beats for $3 billion
t.zh: 苹果宣布以 30 亿美元收购 Beats

summary.en: Apple announced the purchase of Beats Music and Beats Electronics for $3 billion, by far its largest acquisition. The deal brought a headphone brand and the streaming service that became the base of Apple Music.
summary.zh: 苹果宣布以 30 亿美元收购 Beats Music 和 Beats Electronics，这是它有史以来最大的一笔收购。交易带来了一个耳机品牌，以及后来成为 Apple Music 基础的流媒体服务。

why.en: Small next to Apple's size, so the stock carries whatever value it added. A +1% on the reputation coefficient for an early move toward the services business.
why.zh: 相对于苹果的体量很小，它带来的价值由股价反映。作为走向服务业务的早期一步，口碑系数 +1%。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Apple to acquire Beats Music & Beats Electronics

t.en: Unveils Apple Watch, the first new product category under his leadership
t.zh: 发布 Apple Watch，他任内的第一个全新产品品类

summary.en: At the same event as the iPhone 6 and Apple Pay, Cook introduced Apple Watch, the company's first new product line since Steve Jobs's death. It went on sale in April 2015 and grew into the core of a large wearables business.
summary.zh: 在发布 iPhone 6 和 Apple Pay 的同一场活动上，库克推出了 Apple Watch——乔布斯去世后苹果的第一条全新产品线。它于 2015 年 4 月开售，后来成为庞大的可穿戴业务的核心。

why.en: Sales show up in Apple's results and so in the stock. The +2% on the reputation coefficient is for answering the question of whether Apple could still create new categories without Jobs.
why.zh: 销量体现在苹果的业绩里，也就体现在股价里。口碑系数 +2%，是因为它回应了“没有乔布斯的苹果还能不能开创新品类”的疑问。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Apple unveils Apple Watch
Wikipedia · Apple Watch

t.en: Publishes an essay stating publicly that he is gay
t.zh: 发表署名文章，公开表明自己是同性恋者

summary.en: In an essay in Bloomberg Businessweek he stated publicly that he is gay, becoming the first chief executive of a Fortune 500 company to do so while in office. He wrote that he gave up some of his privacy in the hope of helping others.
summary.zh: 他在《彭博商业周刊》发表文章，公开表明自己是同性恋者，成为第一位在任内这样做的《财富》500 强公司 CEO。他写道，自己放弃一部分隐私，是希望能帮到别人。

why.en: A public statement he chose to make, with no effect on Apple's results, so it is a pure reputation event. It was widely covered and broadly well received, and the reputation coefficient gets +3%.
why.zh: 这是他本人选择作出的公开表态，对苹果业绩没有影响，属于纯声誉事件。此事报道广泛、反响总体正面，口碑系数 +3%。

src.name: Bloomberg Businessweek · Tim Cook Speaks Up (2014-10-30)
Wikipedia · Tim Cook

t.en: Says he plans to give away his wealth
t.zh: 表示计划捐出自己的财富

summary.en: In a Fortune profile he said he intends to give away all his money after paying for his nephew's college education, and that he had already begun donating quietly.
summary.zh: 在《财富》杂志的一篇人物报道中，他表示在负担完侄子的大学学费后，打算捐出自己所有的钱，并且已经在低调地开始捐赠。

why.en: A statement of intent, not a transfer, so financial capital does not move. Later share gifts are small and are absorbed in the ownership estimate. The reputation coefficient gets +2%.
why.zh: 这是意向表态而非资产转移，金融资本不变。此后的股票捐赠金额不大，已包含在持股估算里。口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Fortune · Apple's Tim Cook leads different (2015-03-26)

t.en: Refuses a court order to help the FBI unlock an iPhone
t.zh: 拒绝执行协助 FBI 解锁 iPhone 的法院命令

summary.en: A federal magistrate ordered Apple to write software that would let the FBI break into an iPhone used by one of the San Bernardino attackers. Cook published an open letter refusing, arguing that such a tool would weaken security for every user. The government dropped the case in March after getting into the phone another way.
summary.zh: 一名联邦治安法官命令苹果编写软件，帮助 FBI 破解圣贝纳迪诺枪击案一名凶手用过的 iPhone。库克发表公开信拒绝，理由是这样的工具会削弱所有用户的安全。3 月，政府通过其他途径进入手机后撤回了案件。

why.en: The public stand he is best remembered for, so it is scored 5. Opinion was split, with law enforcement and some politicians sharply critical, so the reputation coefficient gets +4% and not the maximum. The stock did not react.
why.zh: 这是他最为人所记住的一次公开立场，因此记 5 分。舆论两极分化，执法部门和部分政界人士批评激烈，所以口碑系数 +4% 而不是加到上限。股价没有反应。

src.name: Apple · A Message to Our Customers (2016-02-16)
Wikipedia · Apple–FBI encryption dispute

t.en: The European Commission orders Ireland to recover up to €13 billion from Apple
t.zh: 欧盟委员会要求爱尔兰向苹果追缴最多 130 亿欧元税款

summary.en: The Commission ruled that Ireland had given Apple illegal tax benefits and ordered it to recover up to €13 billion plus interest. Cook rejected the finding in an open letter. After years of appeals, the EU's top court upheld the order in September 2024.
summary.zh: 欧盟委员会裁定爱尔兰给予苹果的税收优惠属于非法，要求追缴最多 130 亿欧元及利息。库克发表公开信反驳这一结论。经过多年上诉，欧盟最高法院在 2024 年 9 月维持了追缴决定。

why.en: The money was set aside in escrow and the cost is in Apple's accounts and share price. A small -1% on the reputation coefficient for the tax-avoidance label attached to the company he runs.
why.zh: 这笔钱早已存入托管账户，成本已体现在苹果的账目和股价里。他执掌的公司被贴上避税标签，口碑系数小幅 -1%。

src.name: European Commission · Press release IP/16/2923
Wikipedia · Apple's EU tax dispute

t.en: Apple becomes the first U.S. company worth $1 trillion
t.zh: 苹果成为首家市值达到 1 万亿美元的美国公司

summary.en: Two days after strong quarterly results, Apple's shares closed above the level that put its market value over $1 trillion, the first publicly traded U.S. company to get there. It was worth about $350 billion when Cook became CEO.
summary.zh: 发布强劲季报两天后，苹果收盘价对应的市值超过 1 万亿美元，成为第一家达到这一水平的美国上市公司。库克出任 CEO 时，它的市值约为 3500 亿美元。

why.en: The gain itself is in the stock. The +2% on the reputation coefficient is for the symbolic answer to seven years of doubt about Apple after Jobs; later trillion marks get no reputation score.
why.zh: 涨幅本身已在股价里。口碑系数 +2%，是因为这个数字象征性地回答了七年来对“后乔布斯时代”的怀疑；之后的几个万亿关口不再加口碑分。

src.name: CNBC · Apple hits $1 trillion in market value (2018-08-02)
Yahoo Finance · AAPL price history

t.en: Cuts Apple's revenue forecast, citing weak iPhone demand in China
t.zh: 下调营收预期，称中国市场 iPhone 需求疲软

summary.en: In a letter to investors Cook lowered the revenue forecast for the holiday quarter to about $84 billion from at least $89 billion, blaming mainly a slowing Chinese economy and fewer iPhone upgrades. It was Apple's first such cut in more than 15 years, and the stock fell about 10% the next day.
summary.zh: 库克在致投资者的信中把假日季度的营收预期从至少 890 亿美元下调到约 840 亿美元，主要归因于中国经济放缓和 iPhone 换机减少。这是苹果十五年多来第一次下调预期，次日股价下跌约 10%。

why.en: Fully priced by the market, so there is no extra reputation shock (rep = 0).
why.zh: 完全由市场定价，不再额外扣口碑（rep = 0）。

src.name: Apple Newsroom · Letter from Tim Cook to Apple investors
Yahoo Finance · AAPL price history

t.en: Testifies at the U.S. House antitrust hearing with three other tech CEOs
t.zh: 与另外三位科技公司 CEO 一同出席美国众议院反垄断听证

summary.en: Cook appeared by video before the House Judiciary antitrust subcommittee alongside the heads of Amazon, Facebook and Google. He was questioned about App Store commissions and rules for developers.
summary.zh: 库克通过视频出席众议院司法委员会反垄断小组委员会的听证，同场的还有亚马逊、Facebook 和谷歌的负责人。他被问到 App Store 的抽成和开发者规则。
